payload.text: hv in vc's window, read by 2026-11-27 09:19Z by date -u, hv's words: "devbin howto: Yes, agreed to all of that." This adopts the design of hv's idea (hv's words before it: "devbin howto {{topic}}" as topics written for LLMs, a discovery mode, a glob that lists matching topics, a "forllms" topic, core topics added over time, and project-local topics) with vc's five refinements. (1) Core topics ship in devbin's lib/howto/<topic>/, because only lib/ reaches a project; project topics live in the project's docs/howto/<topic>/, and a config key can move that path. (2) Each topic has one entry file, index.md, with a short header (a one-line summary and keywords); the verb prints it after a first line that names the topic's source (core at devbin x.y.z, or the project path). (3) `devbin howto` lists every topic with its name, source and summary; an exact name prints the topic; a glob lists the topics whose name, summary or keywords match; a word that matches nothing lists the nearest names and exits non-zero; a near match is listed, never printed. (4) A project topic overrides a core topic of the same name; the list shows both and marks the winner; --core prints the core copy. (5) forllms is a reserved core topic: how to find, read and follow a howto, how to report back, how to propose a new one, and that hv's words and the project's own rules win over any howto. The first topics are forllms and closeout. cc builds the verb and its tests (M); vc writes the two topic texts; dc proves; vc cuts devbin 0.1.36 and sweeps it, today if nothing goes red (decision 341). A follow-up for Intent: a line in its AGENTS.md template that points every Claude at `devbin howto forllms`.
